verses.1: And the Philistines fought against Israel. The people of Israel were defeated by the Philistines, and they became refugees in the Mount Gilboa.
verses.2: And the Philistines allied themselves with Shaul and his sons. They attacked Jehunanan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua, who were sons of Shaul.
verses.3: The war ended with Shaul. The soldiers found him in a situation of great distress. He suffered greatly from the hardships they put him through.
verses.4: And Shaul said to those who carried his load, “Toss them overboard! Then they will be destroyed. They will not be able to come back, and they will be destroyed by me. I won’t carry their load anymore, because I fear too much.” So Shaul took the load and threw it overboard.
verses.5: And Nebuchadnezzar saw that Shaul had died, and he also fell down on his face. He died along with him.
verses.6: Shaul and his three sons died, and all of his people were also taken away that day.
verses.7: And the people of Israel saw that there were people living across the Jordan River. They tried to attack them, but Shaul and his sons died. Then they left their cities and went away. They became enemies of the Philistines, and they settled in their land.
verses.8: And in the afternoon, the Philistines came to capture the captives. They found Shaul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
verses.9: And they cut off their heads, and they removed all their limbs. Then they sent them into the land of Philistines, around the house of their sorrow, along with the people there.
verses.10: And they placed all of them in a house of idols. And their idols were kept in the house of Shan.
verses.11: And the people of Yabesh Gilad heard what the Philistines had done to Shaul.
verses.12: And every one of them got up and went out for the entire night. They took the land of Sheol and all its inhabitants from the kingdom of Shechem. Then they came to Yabshah and burned that place down.
verses.13: And they took their bodies and buried them under the ashes in Yaveshah. They did this for seven days.
